findings.issue_text: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` in addGuests.handler.ts:38 uses `&&` instead of `||`, requiring a user to be both team admin AND team owner simultaneously to manage guests on team bookings.

`sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` in addGuests.handler.ts:166 passes the raw `guests` array instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`, causing existing or blacklisted attendees to receive the wrong email notification.
`isInvalidEmail` in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:50 is set to `true` on validation failure but never reset to `false` on success, causing the error message to persist after correction.
The catch block in addGuests.handler.ts:171 logs a static string without including the actual error object `err`, making debugging impossible.
No tests exist for the new `addGuests` handler, `AddGuestsDialog`, `MultiEmail` component, or the new email templates, representing a significant test gap.

`ZAddGuestsInputSchema` is defined inside the component body in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:21, causing the Zod schema and its `Set`-creating `refine` callback to be recreated on every render; it should be hoisted to module scope.

`sendAddGuestsEmails` in email-manager.ts:538 sends an `OrganizerAddGuestsEmail` to the organizer unconditionally and then iterates team members, causing a duplicate email if the organizer is included in `team.members`.

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` in addGuests.handler.ts:38 uses `&&` instead of `||`, requiring a user to be both team admin AND team owner simultaneously to manage guests on team bookings.
matched_golden_ids: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same permission logic bug: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` incorrectly uses `&&` instead of `||`, forcing users to be both admin and owner rather than either one to have access.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` in addGuests.handler.ts:166 passes the raw `guests` array instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`, causing existing or blacklisted attendees to receive the wrong email notification.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering out emails that are already attendees and any blacklisted emails, and only `uniqueGuests` are actually persisted. However, the email logic calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the raw input `guests`. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` check determines which template each attendee receives. If the caller included an email that was already an attendee in the input list, that attendee will incorrectly be treated as a “new guest” and receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Blacklisted emails won’t be in `calendarEvent.attendees` (since they weren’t added), so they won’t receive emails, but the existing-attendee misclassification is a real correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `isInvalidEmail` in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:50 is set to `true` on validation failure but never reset to `false` on success, causing the error message to persist after correction.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `AddGuestsDialog`, `setIsInvalidEmail(true)` is called in `handleAdd` when `ZAddGuestsInputSchema.safeParse(multiEmailValue)` fails, but there is no corresponding `setIsInvalidEmail(false)` when validation succeeds. On the success path, it calls `addGuestsMutation.mutate(...)` without clearing the flag, and even in the mutation `onSuccess` handler it closes the dialog and resets `multiEmailValue` but does not reset `isInvalidEmail`. As a result, after the user fixes the emails and clicks Add again, the error message can remain visible until the dialog closes, and it can also persist across dialog re-open since the state isn't cleared on success (only on Cancel).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The catch block in addGuests.handler.ts:171 logs a static string without including the actual error object `err`, making debugging impossible.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the `catch (err)` block after `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` only executes `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and does not log or otherwise surface the caught `err` (nor rethrow). This is directly verifiable in the diff and reduces observability/debuggability of email-sending failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests exist for the new `addGuests` handler, `AddGuestsDialog`, `MultiEmail` component, or the new email templates, representing a significant test gap.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new functionality (handler, dialog, UI component, email templates) and does not add or modify any test files, so you can say this PR doesn’t include new tests. However, the finding claims “no tests exist” for these pieces, which is not verifiable from the diff alone (tests could already exist elsewhere), and missing tests is a quality/process concern rather than a concrete bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` is defined inside the component body in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:21, causing the Zod schema and its `Set`-creating `refine` callback to be recreated on every render; it should be hoisted to module scope.

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx the Zod schema `const ZAddGuestsInputSchema = z.array(...).refine(...)` is indeed declared inside the React component, so it will be re-instantiated on every render. However, this is a minor performance/style concern rather than a clear bug/correctness/security defect introduced by the diff. Also, the `Set` is created when the refine function executes during validation, not on every render just because the schema is re-created. Nothing in the diff shows this causing incorrect behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `sendAddGuestsEmails` in email-manager.ts:538 sends an `OrganizerAddGuestsEmail` to the organizer unconditionally and then iterates team members, causing a duplicate email if the organizer is included in `team.members`.

adjudication.rationale: In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the code always queues one `OrganizerAddGuestsEmail` with no `teamMember` (so it will send to `calendarEvent.organizer.email`), and then, if `calendarEvent.team?.members` exists, it loops over all `team.members` and queues another `OrganizerAddGuestsEmail` per member (sent to `teamMember.email`). There is no de-duplication or check to skip the organizer if they are present in `team.members`, so if the organizer is included in that list, they will receive the organizer email twice.
